title: Console API: model release notes feed + per-model change history endpoints
author: Jada Williams
release_notes: Console users can view a unified release notes feed for model promotions/metadata changes with deployment/region filtering.
Console users can view per-model change history with cursor pagination.
Internal-only notes/fields are now gated by RBAC and never returned to standard Console roles.
body: Summary This PR adds the Console backend endpoints needed by the new “Release notes” feed and per-model “Change history” UI. It exposes a consistent, cursor-paginated API over the changelog generator artifacts/events, with filtering by deployment mode (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), region, category, severity, model, and time window. It also enforces RBAC so internal-only fields never leak to standard Console roles (aligns with ENG-9825 + prior hotfix learnings). Motivation Customers/support have asked for an authoritative per-model history to explain output drift and to correlate rollouts with regressions (SUP-28429). Today model/version changes are visible in scattered places (registry, docs, release process), and there’s no single feed in Console with correct redaction. These endpoints are designed to be the single integration surface for Console (and later, SDK) to retrieve customer-visible notes and audit-relevant details without exposing internal commentary. What’s included API Endpoints (internal Console API) 1) GET /console/v1/release-notes Returns a feed of customer-visible model change entries. Query params: deployment=hosted|dedicated|private (optional; if omitted returns union filtered by caller entitlements), region (optional), model_id (optional), category=security|breaking|perf|quality|bugfix|deprecation (optional; supports multiple), severity=info|minor|major|critical (optional), since=RFC3339 (optional), until=RFC3339 (optional), limit (default 50, max 200), cursor (opaque). Ordering: published_at desc, tie-breaker by event_id desc for stability. Response includes: entry_id, published_at, model_id, model_display_name, model_version (semver), change_type (promotion|metadata_update|deprecation|rollback), category, severity, public_summary (one-liner), public_details (templated paragraphs), links (docs URL, rollback guidance URL when present), affected_deployments, affected_regions (when applicable). Note: internal fields are not present in the schema returned to non-admin roles. 2) GET /console/v1/models/{model_id}/change-history Returns the change timeline for a specific model (all changes, not just promotions), filtered by deployment/region/time and paginated. Query params: deployment, region, include_deprecations=true|false (default true), include_rollbacks=true|false (default true), since/until, limit/cursor. Response includes: events[] where each item is the same canonical “release note entry” shape but scoped to the model; the endpoint can return entries that have no customer-visible release note (e.g., internal-only metadata edits) only when caller has admin/support-internal role. RBAC + redaction RBAC policy checks are done in the Console API layer before assembling the response: Standard Console roles (console_user, console_readonly) receive only public fields and only entries marked publish_state=public. console_admin and support_internal can request include_internal=true and will receive internal_summary/internal_details, operator attribution (actor_id, actor_email), and internal links (runbook, event payload trace). include_internal=true is ignored (and logged) for non-privileged roles. This PR intentionally avoids “best effort” redaction on the frontend; the backend never returns internal-only keys unless authorized. This is to prevent repeat of the class of issue fixed in pr-18463. Pagination Cursor is an opaque base64-encoded token over (published_at, event_id) and request filter hash. We validate the filter hash to prevent cursor reuse across different queries (avoid confusing pagination bugs in the Console UI). Max page size is enforced server-side. Data source / consistency Reads from changelog-generator materialized view (control plane DB table changelog_entries) that is populated from model metadata change events. Note: eventual consistency is expected (seconds to a few minutes); responses include source_watermark_at to help UI message “updates may take a few minutes”. Observability Adds metrics: console_changelog_list_requests_total{result,role}, console_changelog_list_latency_ms, console_changelog_redaction_dropped_fields_total, console_changelog_cursor_invalid_total. Adds structured logs on denied include_internal attempts (without logging the internal content). Security considerations - No internal-only fields are returned unless RBAC allows it. - Audit-relevant fields (actor identity, raw event payload link) are restricted to admin/support-internal. - We do not return customer IDs in feed responses. - Queries are scoped by org_id from auth context; model_id access is additionally checked against entitlements (Dedicated/Private deployments). Implementation notes - New query builder ensures all filtering happens in SQL to avoid N+1 fanout. - Introduces shared “ChangelogEntryDTO” mapping with explicit allowlists for public vs internal fields. - Adds OpenAPI updates for the two endpoints and a shared pagination schema. Testing - Unit tests: RBAC matrix (roles x include_internal flag), cursor stability across pages, filter hash mismatch handling, category filtering, time window boundaries. - Integration tests: seeded changelog entries across deployments and regions; verifies entitlement scoping (e.g., Dedicated-only org doesn’t see Hosted entries for models they don’t have). - Regression test: ensures internal_summary/internal_details keys never appear in JSON for standard roles (covers pr-18463 class). Follow-ups (not in this PR) - Add “account-level recent changes” endpoint for support workflows (see support thread; likely separate ticket). - Add caching layer once usage patterns are confirmed (currently relies on DB indices + pagination). - Expose to SDK after we finalize public API shape (ENG-9823/SDK PRs). Checklist - [x] OpenAPI updated + reviewed - [x] RBAC enforcement and tests - [x] Pagination + filter hash validation - [x] Metrics + logs - [x] Docs stub for Console API consumers (internal) Notes to reviewers Please focus on (1) RBAC/field allowlisting, (2) cursor semantics and filter hash, and (3) entitlement scoping for Dedicated/Private. I left inline comments in ChangelogEntryMapper where the allowlists are defined.

console-api: add per-model change history endpoint + shared DTO
rbac: gate internal fields and publish_state filtering

review_conversation: Chloe Martin: API shape looks good. Two questions: (1) Are we stable-sorting when published_at ties? (2) Can we ensure cursor reuse across different filters fails fast? I’ve seen this become a UI footgun.
Jada Williams (author): Yep. Ordering is published_at desc then event_id desc. Cursor includes a filter_hash; if mismatch we 400 with error_code=CURSOR_FILTER_MISMATCH (tests added).

Nora Ahmed: Please double-check that public feed never returns entries with publish_state=internal even if they match filters. Also, can we make include_internal ignored (not errored) for non-admin to reduce UX friction?

Jada Williams (author): Good call. Public endpoints always add WHERE publish_state = 'public' unless role allows internal. For include_internal, we ignore + log (no error) for non-privileged roles; response contains public fields only.

Jordan Lee: Entitlement scoping: for Dedicated orgs, do we ever show Hosted entries for the same base model if the org isn’t entitled? The UI spec implied scoping by deployment availability + org entitlements.

Jada Williams (author): Correct. The query is scoped by org entitlements; deployment filter defaults to the caller’s enabled deployments. If deployment is explicitly provided but caller isn’t entitled, we 403 with error_code=DEPLOYMENT_NOT_ENTITLED.
Marcus Lin: Security: ensure we don’t return actor_email or internal links to non-admin. Also make sure logs on denied include_internal don’t include any internal content or raw payload.
Jada Williams (author): Confirmed. Mapper has explicit allowlists; actor_* fields are only included in internal view. Denied include_internal logs only role/org_id/request_id and endpoint name.
Dylan Brooks: Perf: Can you add an index to support the published_at/event_id ordering? Also please avoid per-row docs link computation (string formatting per row is OK, but no remote calls).
Jada Williams (author): Added composite index (org_id, published_at desc, event_id desc). Links are computed via deterministic URL templates; no remote calls.
Chloe Martin: Requested changes: Rename ‘since/until’ to ‘published_since/published_until’ to avoid confusion with ‘created_at’ in other endpoints. Also ensure OpenAPI reflects max limit 200.
Jada Williams (author): Updated param names to published_since/published_until across code + OpenAPI, and enforced max limit in request validation.
